tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. action.description: What to do. N="/Users/krk/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_a7e73af0-9f5d-4e4f-a9ef-0e217b5087ac"; cat > "$N/watch-write-lock-contention.md" <<'EOF'
# Watch daemon write.lock contention: root cause and fix (session inspiring-wright-68270a)

## Root cause (verified)
- `brainWriteLockTimeout` is 10s (internal/cli/brain.go:33), shared by every `withBrainWriteLock` caller (375 per `entire graph impact`), including interactive commands.
- Each tick runs: delta -> reconcile -> refresh. `reconcileMemoryAndLaunch` (memory_cmd.go) spawns a detached `entire-brain memory worker --once`. That worker's prepass (`runRefreshDeltaStats` with export: runExport + buildHistoryShortTermLockedContext, both under write.lock) and projection publish hold write.lock for 12-25s on this brain (a full pass is ~2m20s per history/work/v1/worker.log).
- The refresh asks for write.lock seconds later (session export, then seed baseline) and loses both 10s waits. The watch log says "held by pid N for 12s..25s" because the hold was already that old when the waiter gave up.
- Proof of holder identity: locks/write.lock.owner and locks/memory-worker.lock.owner both named pid 57068 (worker started 10:07:23Z, write.lock stamped 10:09:39Z). The watch's own delta step, which runs BEFORE the launch, succeeded on 686 of 724 ticks; the refresh, which runs AFTER the launch, failed on 576.
- Why every tick: the delta reports "14 transcripts failed to scan" on 652 ticks, so every tick is a "repair" tick: reconcile fires (worker launched) and the heavy refresh runs every tick (the repair backoff counter only advances on a SUCCESSFUL refresh, so it never backs off while the refresh keeps losing).
- "seed baseline failed" (652) is the same lock timeout inside the seed stage. "dirty_worktree" (91) is expected behaviour while the tree has uncommitted edits (issue #327) and the tick continues past it.
- The 21 long holds (15m37s, 1m4s) are a different holder (likely a distill pass or backfill); the retry does not cover them, the pending-work fallback does.

## Fix (internal/cli/watch.go only)
1. Worker launch (reconcile) moved AFTER the refresh outcome via a deferred closure with a ran-guard (same pattern as runFactsSync). Still runs once on every exit path.
2. `watchRefreshWithLockRetry`: refresh retried up to 3 times on lock-timeout errors only (errFileLockTimeout or "brain_locked:"), waits 15s/30s/60s, capped at --interval, ctx-aware; injectable `steps.sleep`.
3. `watchPendingAgentWorkUsable`: if every attempt loses, pending distill/seed set by an earlier successful refresh (within one --distill-every window) still runs; reserve is called with the cursor's own fingerprint so the refresh cursor is not advanced.
The 10s global timeout was deliberately not changed.

## Follow-ups (not done here)
- Why 14 transcripts fail to scan every tick (makes every tick a repair tick and launches a worker per tick).
- Memory worker holds write.lock across the whole short-term build in its prepass; shortening that hold would reduce contention for everyone (hooks, MCP, brief).
EOF
echo written

cd "/Users/krk/Desktop/GitStore/entire-brain/.claude/worktrees/inspiring-wright-68270a" && git add internal/cli/watch.go internal/cli/watch_test.go && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Stop the watch tick losing write.lock to the worker it just launched

The supervised watch daemon lost locks/write.lock on 576 of 724 ticks over
20 days on one machine, and because a failed refresh skips the tick's agent
work, the 24h-gated distill ran three times in those 20 days.

Root cause: each tick ran delta -> reconcile -> refresh. The reconcile step
spawns a detached `memory worker --once`, whose prepass export and
projection publish hold the brain write lock for 12-25s on a real brain.
The heavy refresh asked for the same lock a second or two later with the
10s brainWriteLockTimeout, lost it in the session export and again in the
seed baseline, and aborted the tick. The lock owner sidecars named the
same pid for write.lock and memory-worker.lock, and the delta step, which
runs before the launch, succeeded on 686 of those ticks.

Three changes, all in watch.go:

- The reconcile (worker launch) now runs after the refresh outcome, as a
  deferred closure with a ran-guard like runFactsSync, so the tick never
  races its own child. It still runs once on every exit path.
- The free refresh is retried on lock-timeout errors only, up to three
  times with 15s/30s/60s waits capped at --interval and cancelled by ctx.
  The 10s global timeout is left alone: it is shared by hundreds of
  callers including interactive commands.
- When every attempt loses, pending distill/seed set by an earlier
  successful refresh within one --distill-every window still runs, with
  the refresh cursor left where it was so the next tick retries. This is
  the same rule the no-change path already applies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1
